title: Scalar chart models commute with further slice restriction
statement:
Let (C,J) be a site with the coefficient-sized smallness, abelian sheafification and locally bijective units needed by the chart model functors [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package, def-weil-size-convention]. For a commutative ring R, a commutative ring sheaf B, phi:underline R→B, and f:V→U, direct chart scalar extension G_V is naturally isomorphic to G_U followed by further module restriction overMap B f [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. The coefficient size is independent of both site universes.

Precise quantified statement, in the contexts recorded by the Lean module:
theorem scalarPerfectChartRestrictionIso :
    Nonempty (scalarPerfectChartFunctor J R φ V ≅
      scalarPerfectChartFunctor J R φ U ⋙
        overMap.{s} (scalarPerfectRingUnderlying.{c, v, s} J B) f)

source.place: Section 03DH and Definition 04IX; parent proof step 4.

proof.text: For a module presheaf on C/U, apply the local sheafification adjunction to the restriction of its global unit. This defines the comparison from sheafified restriction to restriction of sheafification. Its composite with the local unit is the restricted global unit. Over.map is continuous and cocontinuous, hence preserves local injectivity and surjectivity; cancel the local unit. The comparison is locally bijective between sheaves and therefore an isomorphism. Naturality follows from naturality of both adjunction units.

At each test object over V, sectionwise scalar extension before or after restriction has exactly the same tensor module. The identity components commute with restriction maps by the pure-tensor map formula. Sheafify this presheaf isomorphism and compose with the preceding comparison. Both maps are natural in the original module, since their squares agree on pure tensors and the sheafification unit is natural.
Apply this natural comparison to the constant module sheaf functor. This gives the asserted natural isomorphism of the actual chart functors.
